page: Amazon Web Services m6in.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture and powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processors. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores operating at a base clock frequency of 3.5 GHz, supported by 54 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware acceleration instructions including AVX-512, VNNI, and AES-NI. System memory totals 128.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, sustaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor.

Hardware integration focuses on high networking capability, featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. The configuration does not include local NVMe or SSD storage, nor does it bundle physical GPU hardware. All storage workflows require network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes, establishing a clear structural design that prioritizes high network throughput over direct local drive I/O operations.

Benchmark results place the m6in.8xlarge squarely within the median industry range across general compute and memory tasks. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,933, a PassMark CPU score of 36,724.04, and a Redis SET throughput of 31.22 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput reached 35.42 GB/sec. Large-parameter CPU inference testing demonstrated bottlenecks on 70B models at 6.22 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of specialized accelerators. These hardware parameters deliver balanced resource allocation suited for network-heavy microservices, enterprise web serving, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD pipelines, and relational database management systems.
